turns.input: *He looks at Bartolomhew, trying to understand what kind of person he has in front of him.*
turns.draft:
The man standing in the square is tall, a head over most of the passers-by, with blond hair gone mostly white at the temples and a trimmed clerical tonsure he has clearly kept on purpose. His clothing is elegant, well-cut cloth in sober colors, but there is something deliberately humble in the cut of the collar, a faint echo of a priest's habit. His face is pleasant, unlined by worry, and he wears an easy, paternal smile as though greeting a nephew he is fond of.

"Blessed morning to you," Bartolomhew says, his voice warm and unhurried. He gives a small courteous inclination of the head. "Forgive me if I intrude. I was passing through and found myself admiring this fine old entrance. Do you know this part of the district well?"

Nothing in his manner suggests hurry or pressure; he seems content to stand in the mild daylight, hands loosely folded, the smile never quite leaving his face.
